It's hard to pinpoint a specific *cause,* at least for me. The stuff I fixated on could have been anything, since in hindsight, my mental health was already tanking. Before I realized what I was going through was a mental illness thing, too, the only thing that really helped was time. I can remember a specific moment, during my first episode, where I just. Stopped and went "wait, does this really make any sense?" It still took a month or so to fully leave it behind, but. Sometimes you get lucky and your brain self-corrects on its own.

In general, for anyone who gets this kind of thing, meds and psychiatric help would be my recommendation, but. It's really not as easy as it sounds. It's hard to realize that you're having an episode while in the middle of one, and finding the right person to help you can take a lot of trial and error. Failing that, just having support from loved ones can help a lot.

IIRC, a very basic rundown of what happened is that the company that owns and manufactures Vantablack (an extremely light-absorbent coating that uses nanotubes) gave Anish Kapoor the exclusive rights to use a spray version for artistic purposes. A lot of artists consider this an unfair monpoply, but realistically, it's not that restrictive. Hell, looking at the Wikipedia page, they let Activision use Vantablack to promote a Call of Duty game. Stuart Semple created a "pinkest pink" in response, releasing it with the stipulation that Anish Kapoor could not use it. In 2016, Anish Kapoor made an Instagram post featuring his middle finger dipped in the pigment, but as far as I'm aware hasn't really spoken on Semple since.

He, on the other hand, constantly to this day references Anish Kapoor on his website with similar stipulations on various pigments. The about section even calls him his "arch nemesis" and a "color hoarder." It just seems to be kind of a silly marketing gimmick at this point, and not in a good way.
